english: "They were counted as shards." Likewise also the race of Israel, when it was unfaithful to the Savior, [says] "as vessels of a potter they are broken, they shall shepherd them with an iron rod" (Jeremiah 18:4); when they were sheep, they were golden and were led under a pastoral "rod", but now "with an iron rod", and "they are broken like vessels of a potter".

Immediately also in Jeremiah a mystical thing regarding such things lies; it is commanded "to go down into the fifth house of the potter, and having gone down" (Jeremiah 18:2) he saw a "vessel" being flattened, "clay" being shaped into a "vessel"; and since the dwelling did not have the form of the "vessel" of "honor", "it fell from his hands"; the potter "let it fall" so that it might be remolded by the potter. Therefore, when a place has capacity for repentance, it is a clay "vessel" capable of being remolded, of being transformed. But when it has reached a stability in a state almost unchangeable or difficult to change, then it is henceforth a "shard". For this reason it is cast away.

Furthermore, the prophet, after seeing in the "house of the potter" the shaping of the "vessel", takes a "small shard" and "breaks" it. And he says: "thus I will destroy the pride of Jacob" (Isaiah 10:22). Therefore they were rejected, therefore "they are cast out". And he says concerning this in Isaiah, of this "broken shard vessel", that thus "it was broken" (Isaiah 32:20) so that "not to be found" is a part of it "in which" anyone is able to take a little "water" or "fire", that is to say, having become completely useless, not even the "water"—the little bit or that still capable of quenching—can be received, nor the "fire" that brings to the "shard" itself hardness.

Therefore: here does he say "house" for the world or the church? For in this too there are such diverse "vessels" "for honor and for dishonor". And that such things are in the church, the divine word says: "remove the evil one from among yourselves" (1 Corinthians 5:13), "vessels of dishonor" etc. Again, "fornication is heard among you, and such fornication as is not even among the Gentiles, that a man has a woman of his father" (1 Corinthians 5:1). And he commands "to cast out" this one. And the church can be the "great house" and the surrounding place. And "guards" of this "house" are those appointed to watch.

english: Worthy of the food... 'the truths were becoming real' (12:3d). And those 'looking in the eye-sockets' will darken. These 'looking in the eye-sockets' are the souls using the senses. For the senses are to be taken as 'eye-sockets'. Therefore, those 'looking in the eye-sockets' will 'darken'. For when the sensible things pass away, then darkness will prevail; they no longer see those sensible things as they ought; is there anything left besides the loss of accurate perception?

It is also possible to take it this way: those 'searching the Scriptures' and 'paying attention to the reading' of them find 'eye-sockets', through which they are able to be enlightened, and the light that exists within. Therefore, these 'looking in the eye-sockets' 'were darkened' because they are no longer 'becoming real'. But the 'becoming real' ones split the seeds, making 'eye-sockets'. Take the investigation of the Scriptures and their clarity by analogy with the splitting of the seeds which makes the 'eye-socket'; and this is also what it means for them to 'become real'.

And it can be said differently: they say that those 'looking in the eye-sockets' seem to see much; and some are able to approach the light; and despite the inability and the weakness of the sight, a perception of the light occurs. When, therefore, the hidden light is produced again, those 'looking' are 'darkened' through certain 'eye-sockets'. They are not able to see the light, having those small 'eye-sockets'. But when their body changes from the 'perishable' to the 'imperishable' and from the 'psychic' to the 'spiritual', they no longer have 'darkening' senses, but renewed and increasing ones.

Therefore, the 'darkening of those looking in the eye-sockets' does not bring complete injury; for when they 'are darkened', they will see things more clearly according to the argument of 'the part', so that their own 'eye-socket' of 'the part' is not 'abolished' by becoming a great opening. And it is possible to take it this way because 'the eye-sockets' is in the plural. A praiseworthy 'eye-socket' is brought forward in the singular in the Mosaic writings, when he received a desire to 'see the face' of God and to see Him clearly and 'knowingly'. God said to him that, being still a 'man', he 'is not able' to possess the brightness (Exodus 33:20); 'but I place you in the opening of the rock' (Exodus 33:22), regarding one 'rock' as an 'eye-socket'. And 'the rock is Christ' from that...

Regarding the 'rock' and the openings in Christ. For they are called 'rocks' in the plural and 'crevices'. 'The spirit crushes the rocks'. And it is said concerning the devil: 'The pride of your heart has carried you away to dwell in the crevices of the rocks' (Job 13:16)—not 'in the crevice of the rock', for that is blessed—but because they pay attention to antichrists and false teachers and false prophets, the 'crevice' of those is not for seeing but rather for harming. 'Fissures of rocks' indeed are called 'crevices' in other places; and the discord of the teaching is a 'schism' and a multitude of 'crevices'. Therefore, those 'looking' in the 'crevice' do not 'gaze darkly', but rather are enlightened. But those in the many 'crevices' who seem to see are 'darkened'. When the truth comes into the midst, every deception is loosed; and in the deception were the many 'crevices'. And as they often said the image of the division, that those failing the vote of 349 say ten thousand 'rocks'. If therefore the correct vote shines upon, that which those voting wrongly said is loosed. Thus those holding false doctrines, in the absence of the truth, become so; when this shines and illuminates, all those holding false doctrines are loosed.

12,4ab And they will shut doors in the marketplace in the weakness of the voice of the truth. 12,4a I spoke concerning human matters, those 'being seen and being timely'. Concerning the coming age and the end of the present age he teaches and says that 'they will shut doors in the marketplace' (Acts 19:41). And 'marketplace' here he means the church, as the rhetoricians say. As long as this life exists, the 'marketplaces' or the 'marketplace', the church, exist, in which those who speak are speaking. But 'it will be shut' after these things, when teaching is no longer present in the 'time of judgment'. english: The five who have gathered oil, pressed from the true olive tree, possessing that which provides nourishment and illuminates, entered with the bridegroom into the banquet when a cry occurred in the middle of the night: 'The bridegroom comes, go out to meet him' (Matt 25:6). But those who did not take oil in the vessels, having neglected the one who guards the light, went out to buy and no longer found those selling them; for it was no longer a place of instruction then, nor were those selling the divine words present. And because of this, they remained outside.

And here, therefore, when the village is gathered, the 'marketplaces' are 'closed'; they do not have those 'open doors' about which the divine words write. For indeed the apostle says: 'A great and effective door has been opened to me, and there are many who oppose me' (1 Cor 16:9). If the 'great door' of the word is 'opened' and 'effective', then 'many who oppose' are present. And it is 'effective' when those who hear convert the teachings into works. And 'many' become 'opposing'; for if we observe the Scriptures, it is not always that false prophets are found when they are prophets, nor are false apostles present at other times when they are apostles and teachers. For, envying, they 'oppose' and attempt to contradict the truth, attempting to contradict those who teach well, sometimes even attacking them and leading them to death. Therefore, a 'door' 'has been opened to me, great and effective'. It is not that the 'marketplace' was 'shut', but the 'doors' of the 'marketplace' were not 'open'.

And in another epistle of his he says: 'After I had come and a door had been opened, I had no respite for my spirit, not finding Titus my brother' (Col 4:3). Before the 'door was opened', he 'had no respite' so as to bring forward the word without finding those who cooperate with him. And in the proverbs it is said: 'Blessed is the man who listens to me, and the man who, if he keeps my ways, remains watchful at my doors by day' (Prov 8:34). The 'doors' of wisdom are the 'doors' of the 'marketplace'. Therefore the 'doors' in the 'marketplace' are 'closed' when the place of instruction is gathered. And see that they 'close' the 'doors' voluntarily. The 'closing' of the 'doors' is not by force.

english: It must be said, because of the truth, what is the inherent nature of things. What then are those 'closing the marketplace'? They are the teachers. This is similar to what is said in Isaiah, though rather according to a different thought than the literal words: 'I am being finished by the clouds so that no rain falls upon it'; for from receiving the 'rain', they were turning the 'thorns' and the 'thistles' into plants, but the intention of the 'clouds' and what was commanded to them was that the 'vineyard might bring forth brief grapes'; but since instead of 'grapes' they had grown 'thorns', not wishing to increase the evil again by stinginess, He 'commanded' them 'not to rain'.

In this way also these [teachers], since they no longer had those whom they ought to teach, 'closed the doors in the marketplaces'. And this happens in this way many times, for when the teachers hear: 'Do not give the holy thing to the dogs, nor cast pearls before the swine, lest turning they throw them upon you and trample you' (Matt 7:6). Toward this, again, 'it is not given to those'. For they were about to be more impious, 'trampling' the divine words which are the 'pearls', [and] decorating the 'inner man' with [worldly] things; not even observing the beauty or the preciousness of them, they were about to 'trample' them instead of regarding them highly. So in a certain way they 'close the doors in the marketplace' here; and if so here, much more there, until the judgment seat and the tribunal be 'opened'.

'And the daughters of song shall rise up to the voice of a sparrow, and all the daughters of song shall be humbled' (Ps 47:6). The 'marketplace' will 'rise up to the voice of a sparrow'. Those 'knowing in part and prophesying' 'closed' the 'marketplace' and its 'doors'. These are the 'apostles', the 'prophets', the 'teachers' among men. Let us show that even the spiritual [beings] 'sent for ministry' are 'withdrawn' 'to the voice of a sparrow'. A 'sparrow' may be said to be the Savior here according to the man, according to: 'And I became as a sparrow upon a roof' (Matt 24:32). And each of the birds, when 'having heard the words' of Jesus, turns them into works and 'builds a house' and fills the building and crowns the building, cries out 'upon the roof' in vigilance.

As if raising the 'voice'. The proclamation of the truth can also be called a 'sparrow' then, becoming lofty, since it once happened below for the hearers. But since now even the perfect hearers have become inspired and pursue the things above, there the 'sparrow upon the roof' cries out to them; the perfect has cried out, happening above the world, to face 'face to face' with the truth.

'Rising to the voice of the sparrow', since it is also possible for them themselves to 'rise' concerning which the word speaks according to the expected resurrection. The proclamation of the resurrection signifies one thing in many ways. For when it is compared to a 'trumpet'—'the trumpet shall sound and the dead shall rise incorruptible' (1 Cor 15:52)—this trumpeter is the herald of the resurrection, calling so that all having heard the summons may 'rise'. For this reason it is compared to a 'trumpet'. And this instrument is loud-voiced and is heard everywhere. Thus also here the proclamation of the resurrection said 'sparrow', which seems not to be undignified.

The 'rising ones' are 'being raised', but instead of 'corruptible' they are 'incorruptible', instead of 'dishonorable' and 'weak' they are 'strong' and 'glorious', instead of 'psychic' they are 'spiritual'. Therefore, there will be a 'rising into the voice of the sparrow'. But how will that 'marketplace' which was 'closed' 'rise'? It will 'rise' in the whole world.

I say this: that proclamation being made public here changes from being 'in part' 'prophecy or knowledge' (1 Cor 13:9) but becomes 'face to face'. This is the 'rising' according to the former dispensation. But what kind of 'time' shall we receive? The time of 'judgment'. But in what 'time' is it 'closed'? When the present age reaches its end. In this... the beginning and the end are one. The end of this day brings the beginning of the next... there is no separating time from time. Therefore, what is called 'now', which they say is noteworthy and the boundary of time, is the end of the past, the future of the present, and again the end of the present and the beginning of the future. If I say this, I say judgment and resurrection together; and it seems that the beginning is the end of the resurrection.

english: concerning the judgment: for we anticipate them being raised, not being judged, even if it happens at once. As I have often said, that the body and the color are at once. It is not possible to say one before the other; for the body is anticipated; it is necessary for it to be a body so that it may be color; for I do not anticipate the color so that it may be the body.

“And all the daughters of song shall be humbled” (12:4d). According to all those things assigned to “shall rise to the voice of a sparrow,” I speak of the “humbling” of the “daughters of song.” The false teachers are “daughters” of “song”; they are “daughters” of “voice” alone, not of mind, nor of wisdom, nor of knowledge, nor of light. And because of their [unintelligible] and because of what has been exposed concerning the “pro kairos,” these “daughters” are spoken of. Therefore these “shall be humbled”; and in the way that darkness is dissolved by the presence of light, so by the presence of “rising to the voice of a sparrow,” or the “marketplace,” or the Savior, or the divine teachers, their nothingness is exposed. It is shown that their teaching had existence only insofar as it lived by the presence of [the moment]—and so that I may say something much more impoverished than what is often said by some—that “human wisdom,” promising eloquence and a composition of words, has existence up to “voice.” And since this “voice” will pass away, no longer being struck air, when they become above the air, those concerning whom the word is spoken “shall be humbled.” The “daughters of song” are found to be nothing, if the wise teachers were not called “daughters” or “daughters of song,” but rather “sons of light,” “sons of wisdom.” Furthermore, do we have something to say from another scripture appropriately? “Turn away from me the sound of your songs, and the melody of your psalter I shall not hear” (Song of Songs 5:6); their “song” is considered a disturbance. And “song” and “melody” are the same. And even “I will turn,” he says, “their feasts into mourning and their songs into lamentations” (Hosea 7:8); behold, an appropriate “song.” And the [text cuts off].

Having said, 'Sing to us a hymn from the songs of Zion,' they were mocking. They said, 'Even upon the rivers of Babylon there we sat and wept' (Ps 137:1). 'Having reached Babylon and its unstable currents called rivers, we sat; we no longer desired to depart, taking memory of their own fatherland. This happened by us remembering Zion; we no longer desired [to depart] before Babylon.'

Then he says, 'Upon the willows in the midst of it we hung our instruments' (Ps 137:2), the musical instruments, the instruments of the new song. And the willows are a plant that is fruitless, deceiving men. They say that if its flower is rubbed into water and drunk, it makes the castrated ones lustful. For this reason the poet said the willows are 'fruitless,' because they castrate the men in a certain way. The instruments, therefore, that is, the bodies, were hanging from the willows, the branches of impurity.

Then they, as if performing a circumcision, were saying, 'Sing to us a hymn from the songs of Zion,' saying 'songs' in the plural more insolently. For one song is that of Zion and one hymn; for it is said, 'O God, I will sing to you a new song' (Ps 96:1), one song. These, therefore, since the discordant [one] makes many songs, are saying this in a broken way; it is said discordantly, 'Sing to us a hymn from your songs' (Ps 137:3).

Then they, knowing that they are saying the songs in the plural badly, [say]: 'How shall we sing the song of the Lord in a foreign land?' (Ps 137:4). 'In a foreign land we are yours' (Ps 137:4). So it is a broken song and a thing to be blamed. And if he says, 'with the singing not to be allowed,' it signifies a broken song, a psalm not being properly brought forth.

'And from on high they shall see and be amazed in the way; and the almond shall blossom, and the thorn shall grow thick' (Jer 31:19). If anyone sees from on high, being called high, having a high heart and a high mind, he sees that 'in the ways there are amazements' (Jer 31:19).

They were deacons of these traditions. And they quickly 'flourished' and quickly withered. But the 'rod', the priestly 'staff', being not present, remained until much, until a succession might be born from the greater and more spiritual priesthood; and it surpassed the others. And this must be said: that there will be a true teaching and a false and deceptive one. For they say: in the times of the prophets, false prophets are found; for the evil is a mimic of the true. From the time that Christ appeared in visitation, many false Christs promised to come.

We say therefore this: even if those of the other teachings were plants, and later 'blossom' after the upright teaching and before it; for when it appears, they are quenched. This 'rod' therefore loosed the 'rods' of the others, of the false apostles, of the false prophets. Will the 'almond' therefore 'blossom'?—this: when 'the daughters of the song are humbled' (Song of Solomon), the promised false teachings, false 'rods', then even more 'the almond will blossom'.

Regarding the apostolic word, we say that there will be a standing of righteousness when injustice prevails among men. Loosing the injustice and revealing those who advocate it, being something great, its greatness would not have been shown if there were not a great injustice which it loosed. And we say that 'the truth of God prevailed in human falsehood'. And we say that then, especially, the good appeared of the truth, when many false sophists came into the midst, promising contentious words.

Let there be a king capable and having a many-handed army and experienced in war. Does his greatness not appear when he goes against an enemy of thirty men and prevails over them? And not thus by the Preacher, but rather by Ezra, were problems regarding the king set forth. And the former two have spoken well, but the second interpretation of the third was strong; and it has been said that 'truth conquers' and is powerful. For even if 'women are strong' and such 'wine' and the 'king' and the others, but 'truth excels'. The 'prevailing' of the 'truth' appeared while those strong ones were present.

english: Having been interpreted by others, they were somewhat obscure, remembering; and remembering this, the magnitude of the 'truth' did not appear. And the 'acris' (judgment) might grow fat. In the apostolic [word] it was said again this: that where there is 'law', there also is 'transgression'. If the gospel had not come into the midst, there would not have been a great punishment according to those not receiving it.

Immediately indeed he says that it is necessary 'that this gospel of the kingdom be preached in all the world for a testimony to all the nations' (Matt 24:14), so that no one might take a pretext to seize the unseemly. When therefore the aforementioned 'almond shall blossom', the 'acris' (judgment) 'grows fat'; and the 'acris' is taken instead of a flogging; 'the locusts consumed the remnant of the field' (Joel 1:4). And it 'grows fat' then receiving much food; and its food are the men being handed over to it. And it is possible also to take as a character the 'blossoming of the almond'.

The 'almond' has two perimeters outside the edible part: shell-like and then bitter, the husk which is on the outside. The outside husk may be the body; for it is bitter, having a relation to pleasure. But that shell-like husk is the soul, for it is well-proportioned and large; and within is the edible, the spirit. When therefore that [thing] of the time of the apostle writing is fulfilled: 'May the God of peace sanctify you wholly, your whole spirit and soul and body' (1 Thess 5:23), 'the almond has blossomed'; for in the 'blossoming' these three things are contained. Therefore the man 'blossoms' when he advances in virtue, having 'the body being transformed' (Rom 12:2) so as to become 'conformed' to the 'body' of Christ.

And the caparis might be scattered, because the man went into the house of his age. The 'house of the age' of the 'man' is the life after these things. All the things spoken are happening: and 'the doors are shut in the marketplace', and 'they rise up to the voice of the sparrow' (Prov 7:23) those being called to this, and 'the daughters of the singer are humbled' (Ps 84:12). Those who are in the 'house' of the 'age' are the 'men'. And the place concerning the earth is the 'house' of this 'age of the evil one'. All the things spoken are happening. Since therefore [he] 'went into' another 'age', [he went] 'into' the age of 'his own house', 'into' that after these things.

All things having passed away here are loosed. It is possible to take it this way also, since the 'man' is according to the soul. When all the things that have come to him are loosed—the fleeting things, the trivial things—he 'goes into' his own remaining 'house,' having left this 'age.' And an 'age' is appropriate and a 'house' is for the 'man' who has become a divine state, being 'according to the image and likeness of God,' from which he 'departed' from this 'age.' Those things are loosed, as if someone says that fornication has ceased. For the 'man departed into' the place of incorruption.

And those being cut in mourning surrounded [him] in the marketplace (Matt 12:5). Therefore, 'after the flute has been played' and 'the wailing' is increasing, those formerly speaking in the marketplace, as if lamenting them, [speak]. Therefore, 'in the marketplace those being cut surrounded [him].' You also have it said in the Gospel by the Savior: 'To what generation shall I liken this generation?' and he says: 'It is like children sitting in the marketplace, calling to one another: We played the flute for you and you did not dance; we mourned for you and you did not weep' (Matt 11:17). And he adds: 'John came neither eating nor drinking' (Matt 11:10). Behold the 'lamenting of the child'; for John is taken for all the ancient Scripture and those who ministered to it, but the Son of Man [is taken] for the body of the Church, the apostolic and evangelical choir. He says, therefore, that the 'children play the flute,' so it is necessary for those hearing the flute to 'dance.' But the 'dancing' of the imitation of words is promised to be made through the hands. When, therefore, they hear the word of the wise of salvation and the word bringing forth piety, and are conformed to the announced works and the intellect, they 'dance' praiseworthily according to the dancing which David 'danced' before the ark (2 Sam 6:14). For when they 'lament' calling to repentance, raising up feeling, they 'cut [their breasts],' because this raises up feeling. When one laments and cuts [his breast] because another is sinning, he immediately says, 'How much this one reproaches himself for my sake, I also ought to do this.' And these, therefore, hearing the lament, if they 'cut [their breasts]' bearing their hands against their chests, they raise up feeling for themselves. These, therefore, [were] the former speakers...

english: And having said many things regarding those who do not listen, they 'are being cut'. Thus also Jeremiah, after Israel and Jerusalem had been taken captive, having sat in desolation, lamented with a wail for the throne. And even so God says: 'Lament for me concerning the bride girded with a sackcloth for her man, the virgin conquering'. Therefore, 'those being cut were surrounding in the marketplace'. The teachers rejoice when the hearers are being made straight; they are grieved when the divine decrees are heard against them. Since, therefore, even after the hearers sin, the teachers pity them in proclaiming the divine, 'those being cut cry out', not seeing those who are doing what they stand in defense of. And the New Testament knows the church as a 'marketplace', just as the Greeks do. In the Acts of the Apostles, indeed, it says that 'they have' certain requests, 'market-people lead them', that is to say, rhetoricians. 'You are able', he says, 'to move a case concerning this, those who are proclaiming, the rhetoricians'. Therefore, 'those being cut surrounded in the marketplace' those who were proclaiming; having been exalted and even 'dancing' after 'having surrounded', [it would be] 360 if what is said by them were being transferred into works of ages. Until the silver cord is not overturned and the golden ornament is crushed.

12,6ab Toward a literal sense: 'the silver cord' may be the giving and the receiving concerning transactions. Toward a spiritual sense: since the word of the Lord is 'silver' and 'his words are refined silver', 'cords' are woven from these; that is, things well-understood by the orthodox or otherwise, both ways, the 'silver cord is not overturned', [it] 'is active'. And since it is necessary to speak regarding the text, this may be said: that 'until the silver cord' 'is active', not 'being overturned', not 'being cast out'—for it 'shall be cast out' after these things, when 'that which is from the part is abolished'—the 'those being cut in the marketplace surround', 'until' they have the 'silver cord', 'until' they weave the 'words of the Lord'; then indeed they also proclaim.

english: To 'give drink to a child' who is thirsting; from that very 'source' she herself drank without 'water'. Thus you also find written concerning the Samaritan woman that she also 'left the water', in which it is written to draw water, 'and she went' to her own citizens to say to them, 'Come, see a man, who said to me all my sins' (John 4:28-29).

Rebecca therefore 'gives drink to the child' of Abraham, and not him alone, but also all those with him. 'And to the camels also' she... while drinking—for she 'went down to the spring'—but even if she carries 'water'... she was carrying, but 'to all' (Genesis 24:18-20).

'That which is known in part' and 'that which is prophesied in part' from the 'source' is 'water' having been filled. When therefore 'that which is in part' is abolished, 'the water is crushed.' And it is not destroyed, but [it goes] into the 'source'.

And I remind [you] of another doctrine spoken through other voices and material signs: we say that 'that which is in part' does not vanish, but is to be 'in part'; for an addition of the lacking honor has become.

"συντρίβει" ἄρα κατ̣' αὐτήν. καὶ οὐκ ἔξω που 362 "συντρίβει", οὐκ ἔξω που βάλλων "συντρίβει", ἀλ-λὰ ······ "πηγὴν" χύννεται τὸ "μέρος" τῷ ὅλῳ ···? τουτέστιν τὸ "καταργεῖσθαι" αὐτο`̣ κα̣ι`̣ τ̣ὸ "συντρίβεσθαι τὴν ὑδρίαν", ἵνα μ̣η̣κ̣έτι "ὑδρ̣ία̣" ᾐ῀̣. καταλλήλως δὲ τοῖς ὀνόμ̣ασι̣ν καὶ πράγ̣μασιν τὰ νοητὰ χρῶνται ταῖς λέξεσιν. ἐπεὶ γὰρ "πηγῆς" μνήμη ········ε̣?ν "συντριβη" "τὸ ἐκ μέρους" καὶ ε·· περὶ γνώσεως ἦν τελείας ······· "συντριβὴν" "ὑ-δρίας" ε·····αλλ· "κατάργησιν τοῦ ἐκ μέρους" ········ τ̣ὸ κείμενον· "τὸ ἐκ μέρους" κα̣ὶ ἡ "ὑ-δρία" ταὐτόν ἐστιν καὶ ἡ "πηγὴ"
english: And 'the part' is used throughout. So also here, when there is no longer a need for the drinking of 'water' by the Savior 'having given drink' and having made in the 'drinking vessel' 'streams of living water' (John 4:14), the one having in himself the 'spring of living water' does not need 'water'. Therefore he 'crushes' according to it.

And he does not 'crush' somewhere outside, nor does he 'crush' by throwing [it] outside, but... the 'part' is merged with the whole by the 'spring'... that is, the 'annulling' of them and the 'crushing of the water', so that 'water' is no longer needed. Likewise, the intelligible things use words according to names and realities. For since the memory of a 'spring' is... 'crushed' 'the part' and... concerning perfect knowledge... 'crushing' of 'water'... 'annulment of the part'... the text: 'the part' and the 'water' are the same, and the 'spring' [is the same].

english: And what is the 'face to face'? We often encounter this, where the presence 'abolishes the partial'. Often we say that [something] is more pleasant for one to hear, from which we would be benefited if we see him; there we 'crush' those things, because we perceive greater [things], we 'cast out' them; we do not set them aside, but rather we 'crush' them into greater [things].

12,6d And so the wheel shall run upon the pit (Ecclesiastes 12:6). It is possible to draw from a parallel 'pit'; just as it is to draw 'water' from a 'spring', so also to draw water from a 'pit' with a 'wheel'. When therefore there is no longer a need to move [it] thus, then 'the wheel shall run upon the pit' and destroys it. And it is also possible otherwise; for each verse is a line, and each line has its own meaning. We say therefore this, that in many...

source_text: τόποις τῆς γραφῆς ὁ ᾅδης "λάκ-κος" ὀνομάζεται. ἴδε γὰρ τί λέγει· "κύριε ἀνήγαγες ἐξ 63 ᾅδου τ̣ὴν ψυχήν μου, ἔσωσάς με ἀπὸ τῶν κατα-βαινόντων εἰς λάκκον". καὶ ὁ ςωτὴρ ἐνανθρωπήσας καὶ θάνατον ὑπὲρ ἀνθρώπων ἀναδεξάμενος λέγει· "προσ-ελογίσθην μετὰ τῶν καταβαινόντων εἰς λάκκον, ἐπεὶ ἐγενόμην ὡς ἄνθρωπος ἀβοήθητος". ἐσταυρώθη καὶ ἦσαν αἱ χεῖρες αὐτοῦ καὶ οἱ πόδες ὡς "ἀβοηθήτου"· "ἤχθη ὡς πρόβατον ἐπὶ σφαγήν", ὡς "ἀβοήθητος". ἑαυτὸν δὲ εἰς τὸ "ἀβοήθητον" περιήγαγεν. καὶ ἐπιφέ-ρει· “"ἐν νεκροῖς ἐλεύθερος", καὶ "προσελογίσθην μετὰ τῶν καταβαινόντων εἰς λάκκον", κ̣αὶ "ἄνθρω-πος ἀβοήθητος" ἔδοξα εἶναι, ἀλλ' "ἐν νεκροῖς ἐλεύ-θερός" εἰμι”. ······ος δὲ δύναται νοεῖσθαι τὸ "ἐν νεκροῖς ἐλεύθερος", τουτέστιν ἄνευ ἁμαρτίας. ‖ 64
english: In the places of Scripture, Hades is named the 'pit'. For see what it says: 'Lord, you brought my soul up from Hades, you saved me from those descending into the pit' (Psalm 130:7). And the Savior, having become man and having accepted death on behalf of men, says: 'I was numbered among those descending into the pit, since I became as a helpless man'. He was crucified and his hands and his feet were as 'helpless'; 'he was heard like a sheep toward slaughter' (Isaiah 53:7), as 'helpless'. And he led himself into the 'helplessness'. And he brings forward: 'free among the dead', and 'I was numbered among those descending into the pit', and 'helpless man' it seemed to be, but 'free among the dead' I am. And one is able to understand 'free among the dead', that is, without sin.
